releases.name: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.117: custom CA certificates for sandboxed commands and opt-in tools for custom agents
releases.summary: Copilot CLI 1.0.117 adds a sandbox setting to trust custom CA certificates for sandboxed commands behind TLS-intercepting proxies, and lets custom agents opt in to tools explicitly. Approving an MCP server's tools no longer also approves Copilot's built-in requests when names clash, and autopilot now asks before launching each extension.

releases.name: Lovable: Contentstack and Webflow connectors, Claude Sonnet 5.5 for app AI, and permanent primary-domain redirects
releases.summary: Lovable added Contentstack and Webflow app and chat connectors (Webflow apps can read and publish CMS items and read form submissions). App AI features can now use Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-Live 1.1 for voice. Visits to a project's other domains and its lovable.app address now get a 301 permanent redirect to the primary domain, which helps search engines treat it as the main address. Business and Enterprise workspaces also get IP groups for API key allowlists.

releases.name: Hostinger Headless: take Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Antigravity projects live on Hostinger
releases.summary: Hostinger launched Hostinger Headless, which gives you a ready-made prompt to paste into your AI coding tool; the assistant then connects through Hostinger Connector, picks and sets up a backend (WordPress, WooCommerce, Hostinger Ecommerce or PocketBase, or a custom stack such as Node.js with MySQL) and deploys the project, with hosting, domain and email on one invoice.

releases.name: ESP ZeroCode AI: describe a device in plain words and get tested ESP32 firmware in the browser
releases.summary: Espressif introduced ESP ZeroCode AI, a browser-based studio for Espressif boards. It writes a product spec from a plain-language description, draws wiring on your board's real pins, builds and reviews a complete ESP-IDF project, tests it in an emulator, then guides checks on real hardware, with nothing to install.

releases.name: Lovable: Cal.com, Ghost, Magento and Squarespace Commerce connectors, plus Claude Haiku 5.5 for app AI
releases.summary: Lovable added four app and chat connectors: Cal.com for bookings, Ghost for posts and newsletter members, Magento (Adobe Commerce) for products, orders and stock, and Squarespace Commerce for orders and stock levels. App AI features can now use Claude Haiku 5.5; Claude Haiku 4.5 retires on 2 December 2026 and its requests move to Haiku 5.5, which rejects some settings such as a custom temperature, so apps on Haiku 4.5 should switch models before then.

releases.name: Devin Desktop (Windsurf) 3.15.14: in-app browser tab
releases.summary: Devin Desktop (Windsurf) v3.15.14 adds an in-app Browser tab that opens web pages, local dev servers and Devin Cloud exposed ports next to your session, with persistent cookies, element and area selection for chat, and agent browser control. It also adds an Insert in terminal button for shell code blocks and split-pane session links.

releases.name: Mellum2.1 Instruct: JetBrains' open coding model for fast agent work
releases.summary: JetBrains released Mellum2.1 Instruct, the non-reasoning sibling of Mellum2.1 Thinking: an open 12B mixture-of-experts model with 2.5B active parameters, built for sub-agents, tool loops and quick edits. It uses about half the tokens of the Thinking variant on agentic coding tasks, and is on Hugging Face under Apache 2.0 with GGUF files and a multi-token prediction head for up to 1.8x faster generation.

releases.name: Go by GoLand in Cursor and VS Code (public preview)
releases.summary: JetBrains released a free public preview of the Go by GoLand LSP, an extension that brings GoLand's Go language intelligence to VS Code-based editors including Cursor: navigation, inspections with quick-fixes, refactoring, running, debugging, testing and completion. Each preview build expires 30 days after release.

releases.name: Pydantic Pax coding agent and Pydantic AI Harness beta
releases.summary: Pydantic released Pax (pydantic-ai-pax), an open-source terminal coding agent where everything is a plugin, including the coding agent itself, plus a beta of the Pydantic AI Harness SDK ahead of 1.0 next month. Pax runs any model, swaps between local and cloud sandboxes, resumes Claude Code or Codex sessions, and in Pydantic's single-run SWE81 tests cost $9.21 a run on GPT-6.2 Sol versus $21.05 for Codex.

releases.name: Vercel Workflow SDK 5.8: new engine, 12x lower step latency
releases.summary: Workflow SDK 5.8 runs on a rebuilt execution engine with speculative execution for retryable steps. Vercel says step-to-step latency is 12x lower (p75 overhead 85 ms down to 7 ms) and large fan-outs use 14x less function time, speeding up durable AI agents. Upgrade to workflow@5.8.0; non-idempotent steps should set maxRetries = 0.

releases.name: Vercel Pro: Standard builds move to usage-based billing
releases.summary: Existing Pro teams no longer include a Standard build slot. Standard builds now cost $0.014 per build minute, with your monthly usage credit applying to build usage, the same model as other build machines. Check build minutes on the Usage page.

releases.name: GitHub Copilot code review billing will default to the organization
releases.summary: For Copilot Business and Enterprise organizations that haven't chosen a billing option, code reviews by licensed members will be billed to the organization that owns the repository from 30 December 2026 instead of using the member's Copilot entitlement. Admins who want to keep member billing should select Member in Copilot policy settings before then.

releases.name: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.116: env setting for every process
releases.summary: A new env setting sets environment variables for every process Copilot starts (shell commands, local LSP and MCP servers, hooks and extensions), with or without the sandbox. Also: a Jump to latest button in the fullscreen timeline, context-size choice in ACP editors, and warnings when a plugin and a standalone MCP server hit the same endpoint.

releases.name: Lovable: ElevenLabs speech and music models for app AI features
releases.summary: Apps built in Lovable can now use four ElevenLabs models (Eleven v3, Multilingual v2, Flash v2.5 and Music v2) with no ElevenLabs account or API key, charged to workspace credits as AI gateway usage once an admin enables ElevenLabs. Not available with EU inference. Automations also now work on Enterprise, so they are on all plans.

releases.name: Claude Code 2.1.332: skills from MCP servers (beta) and a PreSkillShellCommand hook
releases.summary: MCP servers can now ship skills, which show as server:skill in the / menu (beta). A new PreSkillShellCommand hook can refuse a skill's inline shell commands as it loads, and a long list of fixes targets freezes from flooding hooks and MCP servers, compaction failures and SSE MCP servers that hung after a dropped stream.

releases.name: Google Workspace MCP servers and CLI (GA)
releases.summary: Google made its Workspace MCP servers and Workspace CLI generally available, giving cloud, web and local agents governed access to Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Calendar, Chat and Tasks with DLP rules, user confirmations and audit logging. A new AI Tools Addendum will require agents to use the MCP servers or CLI instead of REST APIs, enforced from 1 February 2027.

releases.name: Devin: Cognition's SWE-2.1 model, plus a 10x-faster Ultrafast version
releases.summary: Cognition's new in-house coding model is trained with reinforcement learning on Kimi K3 and roughly doubles SWE-2's scores on Terminal-Bench 4.1 (50.0 vs 24.2) and FrontierCode 2.0 (41.3 vs 24.1). SWE-2.1 Ultrafast runs the same model at 10x the speed through a Cerebras partnership, and a more permissive SWE-2.1 Cyber version powers Devin Security scans.

releases.name: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.115: Gemini 4 Hydrogen, GPT-6.2 Astra and custom provider models
releases.summary: The model picker adds Gemini 4 Hydrogen (with Extra High reasoning where available), GPT-6.2 Astra and MAI-Code-2-Flash, and you can add and manage your own provider models from /model. Windows sandbox package queries are now on by default, and timeline items can show timestamps.

releases.name: Google Antigravity adds MCP Apps
releases.summary: MCP tools can now render interactive HTML views in Antigravity instead of raw JSON: inline in chat, as a side-panel tab, as a full page in the sidebar, or as a custom viewer for a file type. Standard MCP Apps work without code changes; launch plugins include Vercel, Datadog, CodeRabbit, Better Stack, monday.com and Qodo.

releases.name: Vercel: agents can manage AI Gateway through Vercel MCP
releases.summary: Ask your coding agent in plain language to create reusable virtual model IDs, set team-wide routing rules that redirect or block requests, and set spending budgets for your team, projects and members. Apps then call the virtual model ID, so you can swap the model behind it without redeploying.

releases.name: OpenAI Codex CLI 0.172: thread links, slash-command Tab completion and Bedrock sign-in
releases.summary: Follow thread links from search results and transcripts to reopen saved conversations and nested agents, press Tab to complete slash-command arguments, and jump between task groups in the agent command center. App-server clients can pick Amazon Bedrock Runtime at setup, and codex exec resume now restores saved sandbox permissions and workspace roots.

releases.name: Lovable: publish to Databricks, auto test users and redesigned security checks
releases.summary: Projects linked to Databricks can now publish as a Databricks App from the publish dialog. When testing pages that need a signed-in user, Lovable can create (and later remove) a test user with your approval. The Security view now shows checks first, and running checks doesn't use credits. Also new: Asaas payments for Brazil and a Paper design connector.

releases.name: Gemini API file slicing controls
releases.summary: Pass PDFs, Office and OpenDocument files, audio and video to the Gemini API and ask for only the pages, sheet and cell ranges, or time segments you need; you're billed tokens only for the parts Gemini inspects. Works across all Gemini 4 models in Google AI Studio and the Gemini platform.

releases.name: Supabase Knowledge Base (supabase.com/kb)
releases.summary: A new open-source home for migration guides (from Firebase, Auth0, Neon, Heroku, Vercel Postgres and more), hundreds of troubleshooting articles, FAQs, tutorials and community guides. Every page has a Markdown version that coding agents can request, and it's wired into Supabase's llms.txt.

releases.name: Claude Ship (beta): Claude reviews, fixes and approves pull requests
releases.summary: Anthropic's new PR workflow pairs Code Review (GA) with two beta agents: PR Steward keeps a pull request green by fixing failing CI, merge conflicts and review feedback, and Claude Approvals approves routine changes under a policy file in the repo. Developers can run the new /ship command in Claude Code. Available on Claude Team and Enterprise for GitHub repos, billed on tokens.

releases.name: Claude Code 2.1.331: Code Mode on Bedrock and Foundry, API check in claude doctor
releases.summary: Code Mode now works in terminal sessions on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry and Claude Platform on AWS. claude doctor gains an API connectivity section, plugins can list optional dependencies, and fixes cover MCP tool calls that hung for up to 30 minutes and /compact losing part of its summary.

releases.name: GLM-5.4: Z.ai's coding model built on a Loop Transformer
releases.summary: Z.ai's new flagship loops 28 layers of its 750B GLM-5 base twice for deeper reasoning, adds vision, and targets "Generalized Coding" such as games, 3D and CAD work. Available now in the GLM Coding Plan, ZCode and Z.ai Chat; API access is listed as coming soon and open weights are promised after safety hardening.

releases.name: Vercel Drives get CLI commands and standalone SDKs
releases.summary: Create, list, fork and delete Vercel Drives with new vercel drives CLI commands, the @vercel/drives TypeScript SDK, the vercel-drives Python SDK or a /v1/drives REST API, without needing Sandbox APIs. Drives still mount into Vercel Sandboxes and are available on Hobby, Pro and Enterprise.

releases.name: Cline 4.1.27: LM Studio API keys and full-length file reads
releases.summary: Adds an API key field for LM Studio servers that require authentication and read-only badges on MCP tools. read_files results are no longer cut to 8k characters (up to 2,000 lines or about 48k characters), and with no saved model the Cline provider now starts on the first free model.

releases.name: Inkling 2 Mini: Thinking Machines' open-weights coding model that runs on a laptop
releases.summary: A 26.4B-parameter (3.4B active) looped mixture-of-experts model that runs its middle layers three times per token. Thinking Machines says it leads open-weights models under 100B parameters on DeepSWE v1.1 (48.2%). The ~20GB checkpoint runs on Apple silicon Macs with 32GB+ memory; weights are Apache 2.0 on Hugging Face.

releases.name: OpenAI Agents SDK 1.0 alpha: Codex as a model provider
releases.summary: The first preview of Agents SDK v1.0.0 for Python adds Codex as an opt-in model provider (CodexProvider), embedding Codex Core so agents can run on Codex with SDK tools, handoffs and approvals. The alpha wheels are available only through GitHub Releases.

releases.name: Lovable: free domain for a year when you upgrade
releases.summary: After a workspace upgrades from Free to a paid plan on the web, admins and owners can claim one domain free for the first year (claim within 90 days of first payment). Covers extensions such as .app and .dev but not .com, and renews automatically after year one.

releases.name: Vercel Functions accept request bodies up to 20MiB (public beta)
releases.summary: Vercel Functions now take request bodies up to 20MiB in public beta, up from 4.5MB, for larger uploads, webhooks and API payloads.

releases.name: Claude Code 2.1.330: easel charts and Enterprise Admin Console sign-in
releases.summary: Adds easel, a built-in mod that draws charts when asked and under MCP metrics results (Pro, Max and, where available, Team and Enterprise on macOS and Linux; switch off in /config), sign-in to organisations managed in Anthropic's Enterprise Admin Console, and fixes freezes after compacting very long conversations and in WebFetch.

releases.name: Lovable: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol for app AI features, plus Paystack and Square connectors
releases.summary: Apps built in Lovable can now use OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra (complex reasoning, coding, research, at lower cost than GPT-6 Astra) and GPT-6.2 Sol (everyday reasoning and coding). New app and chat connectors: Paystack for card, bank transfer and mobile money payments in several African countries, and Square for payment links, card charges, refunds and orders.

releases.name: OpenAI Codex CLI 0.171: GPT-6.2 Sol by default and TUI workspace
releases.summary: Adds GPT-6.2 Sol and Astra to the model catalog with Sol as the default selection, turns on the TUI workspace by default (searchable document and image previews and subagent transcripts beside the chat), adds undo and redo in the prompt composer, and codex exec --remote for sessions on an existing app server.

releases.name: DreamCoder: coding harness and IDE from the author of Mastering Emacs
releases.summary: Mickey Petersen released DreamCoder, a coding harness with a tiling window manager that runs in your browser on Windows, Mac and Linux. It has background sub-agents, MCP servers, your own agents and terminals beside chats.

releases.name: Genie 4 in the Gemini API (GA)
releases.summary: Google's Genie 4 world model is generally available on the Gemini Interactions API (v1beta) and in Google AI Studio, streaming steerable 720p, 24fps worlds with synchronised audio from a text prompt, a reference image or both. Paid tier only, at about $0.10 per second of video output.

releases.name: Lovable keeps working while you answer its questions
releases.summary: When Lovable asks you a question it now carries on building the parts that don't depend on your answer and picks an option for the rest, reworking it if you choose differently. It still waits before hard-to-undo steps such as deleting data.

releases.name: Vercel CLI: agents find commands with vercel help search
releases.summary: Coding agents can run vercel help search and describe a task in plain language to find the right Vercel CLI command; add --with-help to also get instructions for the best match.

releases.name: GitHub Copilot connectors: Supabase, Box, Calendly and more (preview)
releases.summary: Copilot can now connect to eight more services through GitHub-verified MCP servers: Box, Buildkite, Calendly, ClickUp, Mixpanel, Supabase, Webflow and Wix. Connectors are in public preview on all Copilot plans; Business and Enterprise admins must enable the Editor preview features policy.

releases.name: AWS Lambda runs GPU functions on Lambda Managed Instances
releases.summary: Lambda Event Functions on Lambda Managed Instances can now run on EC2 G-series GPU instances, deployed as container images, with base images for vLLM, SGLang and PyTorch. You pay the EC2 On-Demand price plus a 9.75% Lambda management fee and $0.20 per million requests.

releases.name: Gemini 4 Neon (Gemini API, Antigravity, Gemini app)
releases.summary: Google's new mid-range Gemini 4 model for coding and agent work, sitting between Carbon and Hydrogen. Gemini API price is $3 per 1M input tokens and $15 per 1M output (thinking tokens included), with a 1M-token context window; not on the API free tier. Also rolling out to paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity and the Gemini app.

releases.name: Gemini 4 Neon in GitHub Copilot (GA)
releases.summary: Gemini 4 Neon is generally available in GitHub Copilot for Pro+, Max, Business and Enterprise users, in the model picker across VS Code, Visual Studio, JetBrains, Xcode, Eclipse, Copilot CLI, the coding agent and github.com. Rolling out gradually.

releases.name: Vercel Board (experimental, all plans)
releases.summary: A shared message board where your agents and people coordinate tasks, with each task's discussion and results kept in one thread, channel-level permissions, and two-way sync with Slack and GitHub. Agents use it through the Vercel CLI or JavaScript SDK; install with npx skills add vercel/board.

releases.name: Vercel one-second static deploys now take CSS, images and fonts
releases.summary: Instant deployments, which put eligible static sites live in about a second with no build step, now accept CSS, images, fonts, PDFs and media alongside HTML and Markdown. Up to 100 files and 25 MB, deployed with the Vercel CLI or API; rolling out on all plans.

releases.name: Google Stitch Loop (waitlist)
releases.summary: An experimental product agent from Google Labs that connects to your GitHub repo and live metrics, suggests improvements, writes the code in a sandbox and opens a pull request for you to approve. Comes with built-in security, latency and accessibility loops. Waitlist open globally, with priority for eligible Google AI Ultra users.

releases.name: Replit Desktop local work and Replit in Microsoft Teams (GA)
releases.summary: Local access in the Replit Desktop app is generally available on Windows, Mac and Linux: pick which folders Replit can use, ask the Agent for changes and review them locally. Replit's Microsoft Teams integration and Microsoft Fabric integration are also generally available, with publishing to Azure in early access.

releases.name: Netlify's new AI app-building experience
releases.summary: Netlify unveiled a redesigned platform that brings AI app creation, collaboration and its production hosting together, so agents, non-technical builders and developers can build and run apps in one place.

releases.name: Devin Desktop (Windsurf) 3.14: Devin Bots
releases.summary: Devin Desktop 3.14.30819 adds Devin Bots: give a Bot an outcome to own in its chat and it plans the work and runs sessions until it is done. The release also adds image viewer zoom and proxy auto-detection for managed enterprise machines.

releases.name: GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol
releases.summary: OpenAI's new frontier (Astra) and everyday (Sol) models, out in ChatGPT, Codex and the API. Astra's API price is 20% lower than GPT-6 Astra ($8 in / $40 out per 1M tokens, $0.40 cached input); Sol keeps GPT-6.1 Sol's prices. OpenAI says Astra builds better-looking frontends.

releases.name: MAI Code 2 and MAI Code 2 Flash in GitHub Copilot
releases.summary: Microsoft's new coding models: MAI Code 2 for multi-file work, debugging and refactors (Copilot Pro and up) and the cheaper MAI Code 2 Flash for quick edits and fixes, which is available on Copilot Free too. Billed under Copilot's usage-based billing.

releases.name: Replit Missions
releases.summary: Set an outcome and a budget and Replit runs a swarm of agents to plan, build, test and iterate towards it, with an independent AI judge checking results against your success criteria. Work stops if the budget runs out; you choose how often it sends updates.

releases.name: Google AI Studio builds full-stack Android apps
releases.summary: AI Studio's Build agent can now go from a prompt to a Kotlin Android app with a Firestore database, Google Sign-In and Gemini API calls that keep your key out of the APK, then publish it to your own Google Play library. Also adds a faster HD emulator and one-click screenshots to the agent.

releases.name: Claude Code 2.1.327: add MCP servers from stdin + /status health list
releases.summary: claude mcp add-json <name> - reads the server's JSON from stdin so API tokens stay off the command line, /status now lists broken agent, skill and command files, and /export asks before overwriting a file. Also fixes project-scope mcp add/remove wiping other keys in .mcp.json.

releases.name: ngrok MCP server (all plans, including free)
releases.summary: ngrok's MCP server is live at mcp.ngrok.com/mcp. Your coding agent can list and explain endpoints, query traffic from Traffic Inspector, write and validate Traffic Policy rules, report usage and search the current ngrok docs. Works on every ngrok plan, including free.

releases.name: Vercel Spend Management: project and product budgets
releases.summary: Set a budget for a single project (optionally pausing just its production deployments when it's reached) or for one product such as Fast Data Transfer, alongside team budgets. Alerts at 50%, 75% and 100%; also manageable with vercel billing budgets in the CLI. No extra cost for Pro teams.

releases.name: Lovable: test database changes in a draft
releases.summary: On projects using Lovable's built-in backend, a draft now gets its own backend filled with example data, so you can test a change that stores new information without touching your live app. Accepting the draft applies the change to the live database and leaves the test data behind. Chats can also now be archived.

releases.name: TeamCity AI Agents plugin: Codex and Claude Code in CI (experimental)
releases.summary: JetBrains' experimental plugin installs Codex or Claude Code on a TeamCity build agent, hands over provider credentials only for the build, and records token counts and the agent's full trajectory as HTML/JSON. Connects to OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter, LiteLLM or JetBrains Air.

releases.name: Lovable connector: Intercom
releases.summary: Lovable apps can now connect to Intercom to search and reply to support conversations, manage contacts and tickets, and search and publish help-centre articles. Add it from Connectors or ask Lovable in a project. Preview comments also got numbered threads and guest replies on shared links.

releases.name: Vercel Token Pass now $150 of tokens for $30/month
releases.summary: Token Pass (Early Access add-on for Pro teams) now includes $150 of monthly tokens, up from $80, for the same $30 per team per month. Covers featured open-weight models on AI Gateway such as Kimi K3, GLM 5.3 and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash; credit resets monthly with no rollover. Connect a coding agent with vercel token-pass.

releases.name: Google Antigravity Dynamic Workflows (/run-workflow)
releases.summary: Antigravity 2.32.0 adds Dynamic Workflows: type /run-workflow plus a task and the agent writes a short Python script that runs subagents in parallel or in sequence, shows it to you for approval, then runs it in the background and summarises the results. Scripts can be saved and reused. Available on Google AI Pro and Ultra in the Antigravity app and CLI.

releases.name: GitHub Copilot to retire six models on 14 Dec
releases.summary: GitHub will deprecate Claude Fable 5, Claude Haiku 4.5, Gemini 3.8 Flash, Gemini 4 Argon, Grok 4.6 and Kimi K3 across all Copilot experiences on 14 December 2026. Suggested swaps: Fable 5.2, Haiku 5.5, Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Gemini 4 Carbon and Grok 4.7. Haiku 4.5 stays for individual subscribers on annual plans.

releases.name: OpenAI Codex CLI 0.169: side-chat tabs
releases.summary: The opt-in terminal workspace now supports multiple side-chat tabs you can reopen after a restart, and you can search older tasks in the agent command center. Codex exec now keeps project config and MCP servers off in untrusted folders unless you pass --trust.

releases.name: Gemini 4 Hydrogen in GitHub Copilot (GA)
releases.summary: Google's Gemini 4 Hydrogen, its latest Flash model, is now generally available in GitHub Copilot for Pro, Pro+, Max, Business and Enterprise users, in VS Code, Visual Studio, Copilot CLI, the coding agent, github.com, JetBrains, Xcode and more. It is billed at provider list pricing under usage-based billing, and rollout is gradual.

releases.name: Replit Performance Agent
releases.summary: Replit's Performance Agent looks for potential slowdowns in your code and logs. Open Monitoring and choose Run scan with Agent, then review and test the fixes before publishing. It needs a paid plan and edit access, and works before you publish. The same update lets admins share projects with individual Viewers.

releases.name: Claude Code 2.1.325: sandboxed Bash now asks permission by default
releases.summary: Claude Code 2.1.325 changes sandboxed Bash commands to follow the normal permission flow by default; set sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed: true to keep running them without prompts. It also fixes a security issue in decoding zstd-compressed responses, and adds prompt suggestions and a Console sign-in that creates no API key in VS Code.

releases.name: Kiro Mobile for Android
releases.summary: Kiro Mobile is now on Google Play, so you can start, follow, steer and review Kiro cloud coding sessions from an Android phone without your laptop staying on. Edited files show as phone-sized diff cards with pull request status; you review and merge in your Git provider. Needs a Pro, Pro+, Pro Max or Power plan.

releases.name: Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Orchestrator in Google Antigravity
releases.summary: Google is rolling out Gemini 4 Hydrogen in Antigravity, plus Orchestrator, a model option where Gemini 4 Carbon or Argon plans and reviews while Hydrogen writes the edits and runs tests, handing back when it hits trouble. Google says Orchestrator got near-Carbon success on Terminal-Bench 4.1 using 24% less quota on average (self-reported). Orchestrator (Carbon) is for Google AI Ultra; Orchestrator (Argon) is for Ultra and paid Google AI Pro.

releases.name: Lovable connectors: Deel and Retool
releases.summary: Lovable added Deel and Retool as app and chat connectors. Deel lets apps read and update contracts, people, timesheets and time off; Retool lets apps manage your Retool organisation's members, groups and permissions and embed existing Retool apps. Add them from Connectors or ask Lovable in a project.

releases.name: Gemini 4 Hydrogen in Cursor
releases.summary: Google's Gemini 4 Hydrogen, the successor to Gemini 3.8 Flash, is now available in Cursor for everyday agentic coding. Cursor says that at its default effort it scores 54.3% on CursorBench, up from 39.6% for Gemini 3.8 Flash. It supports low, medium, high (default) and xhigh effort. It's a third-party model, so it isn't part of the usage included with Cursor plans.

releases.name: Claude Code 2.1.323: Code Mode (experimental)
releases.summary: Claude Code 2.1.323 adds Code Mode, an experimental opt-in in which Claude writes JavaScript to call its tools rather than invoking them one at a time. Organisations can turn it off. The release also lets plugins declare a supported Claude Code version range, and adds a menu when a model needs usage credits that are off or used up.

releases.name: Replit Agent can buy supplies and run Google Ads
releases.summary: Replit Agent can now buy supplies for your business and help you run Google Ads, without leaving Replit. Purchases use Link (by Stripe) and Visa: Agent prepares the checkout and waits for you to approve the total before anything is charged. Agentic Commerce is for Core and Pro users, starting in the US and limited to one-time purchases. For ads, Agent can draft copy, images and a budget across Google Search, YouTube, Display and Discover, and you approve before it launches.

releases.name: Claude Meetings (beta)
releases.summary: Anthropic is rolling out Claude Meetings in beta on Team and Enterprise plans. You can add Claude to a Google Meet call as a visible participant that takes notes, answers questions, and builds docs, whiteboards and other artifacts during the call. Support for other video platforms is coming later. During the beta, notes and transcripts are free; artifacts Claude makes on the call are free through 10 February 2027.

releases.name: v0: Meta's Astryx design system
releases.summary: Meta's Astryx design system is now available in v0. You can select it for a project and v0 builds with Astryx's components, patterns and templates in context.

releases.name: Lovable Automations
releases.summary: Automations let Lovable take care of recurring work, such as a morning check of your published sites, a weekly summary of new signups, or a Friday list of the oldest items in your backlog. Ask for one in Chats and say how often, and Lovable posts what it finds there. Available on Free, Pro and Business plans, and each run is chat usage.

releases.name: Qwen Code 1.0 Preview
releases.summary: Alibaba's Qwen team released a v1.0.0-preview of Qwen Code that merges the agent capabilities of its Qoder coding tool and the open-source Qwen Code CLI into one agent for understanding, implementing, debugging and testing code. You can sign in with a Qwen or Qoder account, and it ships native installers for macOS, Linux and Windows that don't need a separate Node.js install. Marked as a preview, so interfaces and behaviour may change.

releases.name: Gemini 4 Hydrogen in Devin
releases.summary: Gemini 4 Hydrogen is now live in Devin Desktop and Devin CLI. On Cognition's FrontierCode 2.0 benchmark, it scores 38.2%, close to GPT-6.1 Sol's 39.0% and Gemini 4 Carbon's 40.0%, at $2.40 per task compared with Carbon's $4.04.

releases.name: Cursor Projects goes multiplayer (beta)
releases.summary: Cursor Projects, where one coordinator directs a fleet of agents on large pieces of work, now lets you invite teammates into a Project to plan, build and ship together. A shared task board shows who's doing what, what each person's agents are working on and the PR behind each task. Rolling out in beta to all Cursor users.

releases.name: Gemini 4 Carbon in GitHub Copilot (GA)
releases.summary: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon, aimed at complex coding, agentic work and secure code generation, is generally available in GitHub Copilot for Pro+, Max, Business and Enterprise users, billed at provider list pricing. Pick it in VS Code, Visual Studio, Copilot CLI, the coding agent, JetBrains, Xcode and more; rollout is gradual.

releases.name: v0 Security Review
releases.summary: Ask v0 to "run a security review" and it checks the code your chat changed (or your riskiest code) for missing auth checks, injection and SSRF, verifies each finding against the whole project, and reports a severity and suggested fix. It only changes code if you agree. Paid plans; uses v0 credits.

releases.name: Copilot in Visual Studio gets a new engine
releases.summary: Visual Studio 2026 version 18.12 runs Copilot Chat on the Microsoft Copilot SDK, the same engine as Copilot CLI, the Copilot app and VS Code. You can steer it mid-task, see each step's results and per-request cost, watch subagents live and point it at folders outside your solution. On by default.

releases.name: Runpod for Agents
releases.summary: Runpod expanded its tools for letting coding agents handle GPU infrastructure: a hosted MCP server plus tested skills so Claude Code, Codex or Cursor can pick hardware, deploy Pods or Serverless endpoints, debug failures and shut things down. Destructive actions need your confirmation; native plugins for Claude Code, Codex and ChatGPT. Set up at agents.runpod.io.

releases.name: Claude Fable 5.2
releases.summary: Anthropic's newest Fable model, now the default Fable model in Claude Code (2.1.321) and generally available in GitHub Copilot for Pro+, Max, Business and Enterprise users. 1M context; API price $8/$40 per 1M input/output tokens, down from $10/$50 on Fable 5.1. Also on Vercel AI Gateway.

releases.name: Boxes.dev (Launch YC)
releases.summary: Cloud environment for AI coding: run unmodified Claude Code and Codex on parallel cloud machines with your full dev environment, using your existing subscriptions. Start agents from a desktop app, phone, Slack or Linear; each agent gets its own machine to test its work.

releases.name: Codenotary AgentMon Live (open source)
releases.summary: Free Apache-2.0 plugin for Claude Code (2.1.308+) with a live dashboard of agent and subagent activity, token and cost visibility, and a 'Done Gate' that checks for failed tests or unfinished tasks before the agent says it's done.

releases.name: Cursor: voice chat with agents
releases.summary: Talk to Cursor agents in a realtime voice call from the Agents Window, IDE, web or Cursor for iOS. The voice agent hands coding work to the chat agent and gives spoken progress updates; runs on Grok Voice, with zero data retention in Privacy Mode.

releases.name: @GitHub in Slack and Teams (GA)
releases.summary: Mention @GitHub in Slack or Teams to investigate bugs, create issues, implement changes and open pull requests from a conversation. Adds Canvas in Teams for reviewing plans, diffs and previews, plus automatic repo detection.

releases.name: OpenAI Codex CLI 0.167: agent command center
releases.summary: OpenAI's Codex CLI rust-v0.167.0 adds codex agents --no-daemon for an agent command center with unread markers, lets you switch backends from the session picker without losing drafts, and adds local image previews plus a Google Cloud Vertex AI setup path.

releases.name: Claude Code 2.1.319: background MCP tasks + deny-instead-of-prompting
releases.summary: Anthropic's Claude Code 2.1.319 backgrounds MCP tool calls that run as tasks, adds permissions.denyInsteadOfPrompting so a blocked tool call fails closed instead of waiting, and ships /claude-api latency-optimize plus CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_FEATURE_FLAGS. It also hardens auto mode behind LLM gateways and fixes sandbox-escape and Bash permission-bypass bugs.

releases.name: Hermes Agent v0.23.0: full Desktop workspace in a browser
releases.summary: NousResearch's open-source Hermes Agent can now serve its full Desktop workspace in a browser tab from your own gateway (off by default). One gateway owns every session, and the release adds /rewind, pluggable delegation, plugin auto-updates and spend limits for paid MCP tools. Check the breaking changes before upgrading.

releases.name: Cursor: Build Live Apps from cloud agents
releases.summary: Cursor cloud agents can scaffold a web app, spin up Postgres when needed, configure Cursor SSO auth, run publish-time security checks, and return a live shareable link. Available on paid plans with cloud agents enabled; local agents cannot publish.

releases.name: Perplexity Teammates (research preview)
releases.summary: Always-on agents built on Perplexity Computer that own ongoing work: they plan tasks, coordinate other agents, watch connected tools like Slack, GitHub and Linear, and follow up on things like PR review comments. Research preview on the web for individual Perplexity Max subscribers.

releases.name: GitHub Copilot in Xcode's coding assistant (public preview)
releases.summary: GitHub Copilot is now available inside Xcode's built-in coding assistant as a public preview starting with Xcode 27.3 beta on macOS Tahoe 26.6+. The existing Copilot for Xcode extension remains a separate option; all Copilot plans are supported.

releases.name: Claude Code 2.1.318: cloud sessions without a repo + sign-in expiry warnings
releases.summary: Anthropic's Claude Code 2.1.318 lets a cloud session on an Anthropic-hosted environment start with no repository picked, shows when a stored claude.ai sign-in ends (in claude auth status and claude -p JSON, plus a warning 10 days before), and adds an effort option for quick side jobs. It also fixes lost --continue history, macOS stalls with many Bash commands, and config and login corruption on shared network home directories.

releases.name: Vercel Security Review (public beta)
releases.summary: Vercel Security Review is in public beta for Pro and Enterprise teams. Once enabled, every push to a connected GitHub repo is reviewed for vulnerabilities, with findings (summary, suggested fix and AI-rated severity) in a Vulnerabilities dashboard, a GitHub check and PR comments. Fix with Vercel Agent opens a PR, or pull findings into your own coding agent with vercel security vulnerabilities. Reviews are free until 10 November 2026, then billed at the Vercel Agent rate.

releases.name: GitHub Copilot in JetBrains Air
releases.summary: GitHub Copilot is now available as an agent in JetBrains Air through the Agent Client Protocol. Pick Copilot in Air's agent picker to delegate coding tasks on your existing Copilot subscription, track several agent sessions in parallel and review changes next to your code. Cloud tasks run in isolated containers through Air Teams and use your Copilot plan rather than JetBrains AI credits.

releases.name: Lovable: download an SBOM for your project
releases.summary: Lovable now lets you download a software bill of materials for your project from the dependency list in the Security view, in SPDX 2.3 or CycloneDX 1.5 format. It lists production dependencies and their known vulnerabilities, so you can hand it to a security or procurement team. Downloading is free.

releases.name: DeepSeek dsh-superagent (open-source research prototype)
releases.summary: DeepSeek's Harness team open-sourced dsh-superagent under the MIT licence: a proactive coding agent for one GitHub repository that listens to GitHub (and optionally Feishu), turns authorised requests into work items, runs each in its own agent session and directory, and replies with results such as pull requests. A web panel shows what needs a person. DeepSeek labels it research code, not production-ready, and it runs as a bundle for DeepSeek Harness.

releases.name: Claude Code 2.1.316: subagent effort control; Opus 4.8 fast mode deprecated
releases.summary: Claude Code added CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_EFFORT to set the effort level subagents run at, a CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ULTRATHINK switch, and pooled group budgets in the Claude apps gateway. Fast mode for Opus 4.8 is deprecated and will be removed on 30 Nov 2026 (requests will error, not fall back); Anthropic says to move to Opus 5.5.

releases.name: Replit Cloud Agents for company codebases (Enterprise) + Agent chat messaging
releases.summary: Replit Enterprise customers can describe a change in plain language and a Cloud Agent finds the relevant code, makes the change, tests it in the running app and opens a GitHub pull request or GitLab merge request with screenshots and video, working in isolated cloud sandboxes for engineers to review. On Pro and Enterprise, Agent can now send messages to other chats or start new ones, and GPT-6.1 Terra is in the model selector for Agent in Power Mode.

releases.name: OpenCode 2.2.3: use your Claude Code login inside OpenCode
releases.summary: The open-source OpenCode agent added a built-in Claude Agent provider: install Claude Code, run claude auth login, then pick Claude Agent in /connect to use your Claude Code login and models while OpenCode keeps its own tools and permissions. Desktop also got faster on long, streaming sessions.

releases.name: Lovable project and personal memory
releases.summary: Lovable now remembers preferences, decisions and facts you state while building and applies them in later conversations. Project memory is shared by everyone who can edit a project; personal memory covers how you like to work across all projects. Memory settings show a plain-language summary you can correct or switch off.

releases.name: Claude Code: block writes outside working directories + idle compaction
releases.summary: Claude Code added a permissions.blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories setting so Write, Edit and NotebookEdit refuse paths outside your working directories in every permission mode, plus idle compaction in VS Code and Claude Desktop's Code tab that summarises long (200K+ token) idle conversations before your next message.

releases.name: Bolt database tables private by default
releases.summary: From 30 October, new Bolt database tables are private by default, so your app needs explicit permissions to read or write data. Existing databases aren't affected, and Bolt sets up permissions when it creates a new database; if you hit a permissions error you can ask Bolt to fix the table permissions.

releases.name: OpenAI Codex CLI 0.166
releases.summary: Codex CLI 0.166.0 adds keyboard-driven transcript selection with search, codex queue --resume for unloaded threads, codex doctor --network-only diagnostics, clearer safety-block explanations, and GPT-6.1 Terra in the bundled, Vertex AI and Amazon Bedrock catalogs.

releases.name: Mistral Large 4 open weights
releases.summary: Mistral released the weights of its improved Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk), a ~1T-parameter multimodal MoE model with a 1M-token context, which Mistral calls the best open-weight model for coding. Download from Hugging Face or use it via the Mistral API and OpenRouter at $0.70/$2.10 per 1M input/output tokens; commercial model-as-a-service use needs a separate licence.

releases.name: Lovable: import apps from Replit, Bolt, Base44, v0 or Manus, or an existing website
releases.summary: You can now bring a project built elsewhere into Lovable and keep building: upload a ZIP export from Replit, Bolt, Base44, v0 or Manus, or enter the address of an existing site, including Wix, Squarespace or Webflow sites. The first import is free; later imports use standard build credits.

releases.name: Factory Droid 1.0
releases.summary: Factory released Droid 1.0, a rebuilt harness for its model-agnostic coding agent. Programmatic tool calling is now on by default: the model writes a sandboxed JavaScript program that can run hundreds of tool calls in one request, keeping raw outputs out of context. Factory reports higher Terminal-Bench 4 scores at lower cost than other harnesses (self-reported).
